acceptance: A text-edit run started while the full run is queued ends with the full run's verdict, without manual re-runs
A failing full run still produces failing text-edit checks
A test covers the queued and in-progress full-run cases
context: Duplicate, dropped on creation day: the behaviour was already fixed by PR #3319 (merged 0e86fbbe8, 2026-10-23 02:06 UTC), which made text-edit verdicts decide once and added ci-text-edit-refresh.yml to re-run a failed text-edit run when the full CI run completes. The observation here (run 39793776095, 2026-10-22) predates that fix. Remaining live verification is tracked by ci-text-edit-fail-fast-live-check-20261023.
description:
Editing a pull request's title or body starts a `CI (text edit)` run whose required jobs (`core`, `docs`, `explorer`, `results-data`, `tooling`) copy the verdict of the newest full CI run on the same head via `scripts/ci_text_edit_verdict.py`. When hosted runners are backlogged, the full run can still be queued or in progress when the copy step polls; the step then fails with `gave up waiting: full CI run <id> is still in progress`. Those failures are newer than the full run's later passes, so GitHub keeps the pull request BLOCKED even after every real check is green, until someone re-runs the failed text-edit jobs (`gh run rerun <id> --failed`).

Observed on 2026-10-22: text-edit run 39793776095 failed all five units after about 1h50m while full run 39793750006 was still running; the armed pull request stayed blocked until the failed jobs were re-run, after which they copied the passing verdict and auto-merge proceeded.

The fix should make the copied verdict converge without manual action, for example by re-running or re-posting the text-edit verdict when the full run completes, or by waiting on the full run's completion instead of a fixed poll budget, without ever reporting success the full run did not earn.
